newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The interbank rate eased slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were narrowly mixed. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 0.45/0.40 percent compare with Monday's yield of 0.60/0.55 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.15/1.10 percent against 1.28/1.23 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.28/99.33 from Monday's close of S$99.32/99.37, September 2001 at S$97.38/97.43 versus S$97.37/97.42 and June 2003 at S$95.38/95.43 against S$95.37/95.42.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 3 2-7/8 percent from Monday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
